native_result.query: In what centuries did we see the highest growth phase of the period between 2000 BCE and 1100 BCE?
native_result.HypoA: Between 1500 BCE and 1300 BCE, highest growth of the period between 2000 BCE and 1100 BCE is seen.
native_result.HypoB: Between 2000 and 1100 BCE the highest growth phase in landscape openness (Belau pollen PC1 openness score, used as a demographic proxy) occurred in the 15th and 14th centuries BCE (1500–1301 BCE), with the 15th century BCE (1500–1401 BCE) as the peak century. These two centuries have the highest mean growth rate of the 100-year smoothed openness score (pollen_grate_100: +0.00189 and +0.00111 per year, ranks 1–2 of 10), the highest KDE growth (g_all_mean +0.00283 and +0.00145; kde_all_mean +32% and +15%), the largest increases in the independent Feeser SMOOTH_MEAN_100y series, and coincide with the window maximum of mean capital z-scores (0.26 at 1500 BCE to 0.94 at 1400 BCE, +0.68), driven mainly by social capital (copper & gold, amber, monument count: +1.53) and symbolic capital (hatchets & swords, daggers, house size: +0.75), with a smaller economic rise (+0.33) and flat cultural capital. Under centred bins the phase shifts to c. 1450–1251 BCE (peak 1450–1351 BCE), so robustly the growth phase is c. 1500–1300 BCE. The 1600–1501 BCE century shows the strongest openness decline despite positive KDE growth.
native_result.WorkflowB: Loaded time_series_data.csv (annual rows, CE=1950-calBP), capital.csv (100-yr, decimal comma) and the Feeser pollen file. Restricted to CE -2000..-1100 (901 rows). Used pollen_grate_100 as supplied (not recomputed; corr 0.89 with first difference of pollen_inter_100) as primary growth measure, aggregated to 100-yr bins via floor(CE/100)*100 (mean, cumulative sum, fraction of positive years); identified contiguous positive-growth runs and the peak century. Sensitivity with centred bins. Cross-checked with g_all_mean and within-century % change of kde_all_mean, within-century change of pollen_inter_100 and Feeser SMOOTH_MEAN_100y, and capital.csv mean z-scores overall and by the study's four capital types (symbolic: hatchets&swords, daggers, house size; social: Cu&Au, amber, monument count; cultural: pottery form, pottery decoration; economic: depot, sickle, axes&celts, monument size). 1100 BCE contributes one row only and is excluded as a century.

native_result.HypoA: During the Middle Neolithic (3400-3000 BCE) and Younger Neolithic (2900-2300 BCE), both phases are primarily associated with negative values on the first principal component (PC1). native_result.HypoB: In a PCA of the 12 forms-of-capital Z-variables in 100-year slices, PC1 (31.8% variance) separates a Bronze-Age pole (positive: Copper & Gold, Pottery Decoration, Depot, Hatchets & Swords, Daggers, Monument Size, House Size, Monument Count) from a Neolithic pole (negative: Pottery Form diversity, Axes & Celts, Amber). Both the Middle Neolithic (3400-3000 BCE) and the Younger Neolithic (2900-2300 BCE) are characterised by consistently negative PC1 scores (MN mean -1.43, range -1.85 to -0.62; YN mean -1.18, range -1.62 to -0.65), i.e. a low-capital, pre-metal position close to the Early Neolithic (-1.74) and far below the Late Neolithic (+0.54) and Bronze Age (OBA +2.95, YBA +1.87). MN declines from -0.62 (3400) to about -1.8 (3200/3000), driven by high Amber (social) and Pottery Form diversity (cultural) with no metal, daggers or depots; YN oscillates (minimum -1.62 at 2800, peaks -0.75 at 2700 with the Monument Count maximum and -0.65 at 2300 with first daggers), driven by Axes & Celts and Depot (economic) and low Pottery Decoration (cultural) with no copper/gold. P1||G0.HypoB: In a PCA of the 12 forms-of-capital Z-variables in 100-year slices, PC1 (31.8% variance) separates a Bronze-Age pole (positive: Copper & Gold, Pottery Decoration, Depot, Hatchets & Swords, Daggers, Monument Size, House Size, Monument Count) from a Neolithic pole (negative: Pottery Form diversity, Axes & Celts, Amber). Both the Middle Neolithic (3400-3000 BCE) and the Younger Neolithic (2900-2300 BCE) are characterised by consistently negative PC1 scores (MN mean -1.43, range -1.85 to -0.62; YN mean -1.18, range -1.62 to -0.65), i.e. a low-capital, pre-metal position close to the Early Neolithic (-1.74) and far below the Late Neolithic (+0.54) and Bronze Age (OBA +2.95, YBA +1.87).
